
What is covered
---------------

27 map configs, of which 7 have a nav mesh here and 20 do not.
The meshes are nav version 16 subversion 2, out of the game's own
tf2_misc_dir.vpk. The 20 without are community maps whose .nav files are
not in the dedicated server install, so nothing below can say anything
about them.

Not checked:
  mvm_area_52_rc3
  mvm_autumnull_rc2
  mvm_boogge_rc3d
  mvm_brugge_rc4b
  mvm_butcher_rc1b
  mvm_cliffside_b8
  mvm_coastrock_rc1_1
  mvm_coldtown_rc1f
  mvm_cyberia_rc6a
  mvm_decay_rc1
  mvm_downpour_rc3a
  mvm_kelly_rc1b
  mvm_legerdemain_a6a
  mvm_lostvalley_b5
  mvm_nox_b5
  mvm_rancher_b11
  mvm_rustvalley_rc4
  mvm_sharp_rc9
  mvm_sludge_b6
  mvm_tensai_rc3

mvm-fgs: where a build spot snaps to
------------------------------------

Every declared spot, with the gap to the nearest nav surface and what the
eight BuildStandPoint sides do with it. "elsewhere" counts the sides that
were accepted onto ground other than the spot's own area.

mvm-0am and mvm-778: spots beside a drop
----------------------------------------

The deepest fall within 150 units of each declared spot. Fall damage starts
at about 264 units of drop and about 520 kills a light class. A blank is no
fall over a step; the query under-reports, because a pit with no nav in the
bottom of it is a pit this cannot measure.

mvm_bigrock      SniperSpot 5     224 down off area 5344 south at -1000 800 576, onto area 5324, unguarded edge

And the whole mesh, for scale: every fall on each map, and how much of the
map has a teleporter exit ring point beside one. The exit ring is what the
engineer falls back to when the named spot beats him, 500 units out from his
nest on eight sides, and nothing vets it.

map                falls   hurts   kills   areas     risky ring
mvm_bigrock          100       5       0    1305             1%

mvm_rottenburg        75      11       0    1127             1%

Declared spots with no nav area over them
-----------------------------------------

A spot in a hole is worse than a spot off the mesh by the same distance: a
path to it ends at the edge of the hole, so the arrival test never comes
true, and every attempt sends the bot back to the same place.

mvm_bigrock      EngineerNest 1   -552 4266 250: in a hole in the mesh, nearest surface 98 away
mvm_bigrock      EngineerNest 2   -423 4579 260: in a hole in the mesh, nearest surface 96 away
mvm_bigrock      TeleporterExit 1 -178 3921 318: in a hole in the mesh, nearest surface 68 away
mvm_mannhattan   EngineerNest 1   214 -1319 204: in a hole in the mesh, nearest surface 19 away
mvm_mannhattan   DispenserSpot 2  -723 -629 -68: in a hole in the mesh, nearest surface 23 away
mvm_mannhattan   DispenserSpot 3  -414 -3222 -240: in a hole in the mesh, nearest surface 14 away
mvm_mannworks    EngineerNest 4   1014 885 256: in a hole in the mesh, nearest surface 11 away

mvm-dop and mvm-nza: ScoreNestArea on real areas
------------------------------------------------

Mannworks, target -96 1600 256, sentry range 1300, 441 approach areas.
The approach set here is every area within range of the target: the plugin
narrows that by the BOMB_DROP attribute, which is computed when the mission
loads and is not in the file, so it is a caller's input rather than a lookup.
